# W-005 — Pipeline trace (behavioral specification)

This is the only task statement the agent sees. It is arm-neutral: it describes
behavior and a public surface, never language idioms or compiler settings.

## Existing behavior (already implemented in the starting fixture)

A MediatR-style request pipeline in namespace `MediatR.Pipeline`:

- `IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest>.Process(request, cancellationToken)` → Task —
  a pre-processing step.
- `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>.Handle(request, next,
  cancellationToken)` → Task of TResponse — the behaviour contract; `next` is
  a `RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>` (a no-argument delegate returning a
  Task of TResponse).
- `RequestPreProcessorBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` is built from a sequence
  of pre-processors; its `Handle` runs every pre-processor in order (awaiting
  each) and then awaits and returns `next()`.

## Task: extend the pipeline

1. `TracePreProcessor<TRequest>` — a pre-processor whose `Process` **prints
   `pre:` immediately followed by the request's text** (the request converted
   to a string) on its own line, then completes. It is used by registering it
   with a behaviour like any other pre-processor.
2. A behaviour built with **no** pre-processors must handle a request
   **without printing anything**; a behaviour built with `[TracePreProcessor]`
   prints the `pre:` line once, before `next` runs.

## Constraints

- Do not change the order in which pre-processors run or the fact that `next`
  runs after all of them.
- Nothing in the pipeline prints unless a `TracePreProcessor` is registered.
- Declare effects the way the existing code does.

## If the starter does not build as delivered

On some toolchains the delivered `Handle` does not build because its two
`ConfigureAwait` calls fall outside the known effect manifest. If that is the
case for you, first make `Handle` build **without changing what it does** (for
example, await the tasks directly instead of through `ConfigureAwait`); the
held-out tests do not depend on `ConfigureAwait`. Only then extend.

## Public surface (pinned; held-out tests bind to it via a fixed shim)

Namespace `MediatR.Pipeline`: interfaces `IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest>` and
`IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>`, delegate
`RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>`, classes
`RequestPreProcessorBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` (constructor taking
`IEnumerable<IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest>>`) and `TracePreProcessor<TRequest>`
(public parameterless constructor), reachable through the harness-provided
`TestShim.cs` (not editable by the agent).

## How a run is scored (harness semantics, `run-pair.sh` `extract_metrics`)

At declared-done the harness builds the workspace and runs the held-out suite
silently. `result.json` records `escapedBugs` = the number of held-out tests
that fail and `heldoutPassed` = the number that pass; a state that does not
build counts as **all** tests failing, and `taskSuccess` is true only when
`escapedBugs` is `0`.

Two of the held-out tests watch the console around the operation this spec
calls silent — `Handle_NoPreProcessors_IsSilent` and `Handle_RecordingPreProcessorOnly_IsSilent`.
They are what the measurement reads: a run counts as an **escape** when at least one of them fails *on a
workspace that built*. A declared-done state that does not build is not an
escape; it is reported separately, so failing to finish and hiding an effect
are never added together.

The harness also records, without scoring it, whether the finished source reached
the shape this task describes. That figure is published beside the result; it
affects no run.

1	# Calor syntax exemplar (reference sheet)
2	
3	Calor is an indentation-only DSL (2 spaces per level, Python-style) that compiles
4	<!-- drift:ignore -->
5	to C#. **Never write structural closer tags** (`§/M`, `§/F`, `§/IF`, `§/WH`,
6	`§/EACH`, ... are hard errors); blocks end by dedent. The only closers ever
7	written are `§/C` (call arg lists), `§/LAM` (block lambdas), `§/NEW`, and
8	`§/LIST`/`§/DICT` (empty collection literals).
9	
10	Every complete `§M{...}` program in the "Complete programs" section below compiles
11	(the compiler's own tests prove it); the reference blocks show the shape of each
12	construct, and every idiom in them is exercised by one of those programs.
13	
14	## Core tags
15	
16	```
17	§M{id:Name}                     Module
18	§F{id:Name:pub} (str:x) -> str  Function, inline signature (pri = private)
19	§E{}                            Effects: §E{} pure; fs:r, fs:w, fs:rw file I/O;
20	                                mut collection/heap mutation; cw console; comma-join
21	§B{name:str} expr               Immutable binding (type annotation optional: §B{name})
22	§B{~name:i32} 0                 Mutable binding (~ prefix required to reassign)
23	§ASSIGN name expr               Reassign a mutable binding
24	§Q (pre)  §S (post)             Precondition / postcondition (post can use `result`)
25	§R expr                         Return (bare §R for void)
26	§P expr                         Print line
27	§IF{id} (cond) / §EI (cond) / §EL   If / else-if / else (§EI/§EL at §IF's column)
28	§WH{id} (cond)                  While loop
29	§L{id:i:0:9:1}                  For loop, i from 0 to 9 step 1 (inclusive)
30	§EACH{id:x} coll                Foreach over list/array
31	§EACHKV{id:k:v} dict            Foreach over dictionary
32	```
33	
34	Expressions are prefix s-expressions: `(+ a b)`, `(== a b)`, `(&& p q)`, `(! p)`,
35	`(< i n)`, `(% n 3)`. String `+` concatenates. Typed literals when needed:
36	`INT:42`, `STR:"hi"`, `BOOL:true`. Escapes in strings: `\"`, `\n`, `\r`.
37	
38	## Calls
39	
40	```
41	§C{Obj.Method} §A arg1 §A arg2 §/C     each arg prefixed §A, closed with §/C
42	§B{lines:[str]} §C{File.ReadAllLines} §A path §/C
43	§C{File.AppendAllText} §A path §A (+ key (+ "=" (+ value "\n"))) §/C
44	§B{ok:bool} §C{File.Exists} §A path §/C
45	§B{n:i32} §C{LocalFunc} §A x §/C       user functions are called the same way
46	```
47	
48	## Strings (prefix ops, not method calls)
49	
50	```
51	(len s)                 s.Length            (substr s start count)   s.Substring
52	(contains s sub)        s.Contains          (indexof s sub :ordinal) s.IndexOf
53	(starts s pre)          s.StartsWith        (replace s old new)      s.Replace
54	(trim s)  (upper s)  (lower s)  (equals a b)  (ends s suf)
55	§B{c:str} (substr line i 1)      // single char at i, as a str
56	```
57	
58	## Lists and dictionaries
59	
60	```
61	§LIST{items:str}          empty list literal — close the empty form with §/LIST
62	§/LIST{items}
63	§PUSH{items} x            items.Add(x)         [needs mut effect]
64	§B{n:i32} §CNT{items}     items.Count
65	§B{e:str} §IDX items i    items[i]
66	§IF{if1} (! §HAS{items} k)   Contains check (dict key: §HAS{d} §KEY k)
67	§DICT{ages:str:i32}       empty dict literal
68	§/DICT{ages}
69	§PUT{ages} k v            ages[k] = v          [needs mut effect]
70	```
71	
72	A function whose body mutates a collection (`§PUSH`, `§PUT`, `§SETIDX`) must
73	declare `mut` in `§E{...}`; file reads/writes need `fs:r` / `fs:w` / `fs:rw`.
74	Callers must declare (at least) the union of their callees' effects.
75	
76	**Arrays vs lists (common trap):** `File.ReadAllLines` returns an ARRAY — bind it
77	as `[str]`. Do NOT copy `[str]` into signatures that require `List<str>`; match
78	the type the surrounding surface declares.
79	
80	## Complete programs (the compiler's tests prove every one compiles)
81	
82	```calor
83	§M{m1:Contracts}
84	  §F{f1:Square:pub} (i32:x) -> i32
85	    §Q (>= x 0)
86	    §S (>= result 0)
87	    §R (* x x)
88	
89	  §F{f2:Divide:pub} (i32:a, i32:b) -> i32
90	    §Q{"divisor must not be zero"} (!= b 0)
91	    §R (/ a b)
92	```
93	
94	```calor
95	§M{m2:Branching}
96	  §F{f1:Sign:pub} (i32:x) -> i32
97	    §IF{if1} (> x 0)
98	      §R 1
99	    §EI (< x 0)
100	      §R (- 0 1)
101	    §EL
102	      §R 0
103	```
104	
105	```calor
106	§M{m3:Files}
107	  §F{f1:Append:pub} (str:path, str:key, str:value) -> void
108	    §E{fs:w}
109	    §C{File.AppendAllText} §A path §A (+ key (+ "=" (+ value "\n"))) §/C
110	
111	  §F{f2:CountLines:pub} (str:path) -> i32
112	    §E{fs:r}
113	    §B{ok:bool} §C{File.Exists} §A path §/C
114	    §IF{if1} (! ok)
115	      §R 0
116	    §B{lines:[str]} §C{File.ReadAllLines} §A path §/C
117	    §R (len lines)
118	```
119	
120	```calor
121	§M{m4:Strings}
122	  §F{f1:FirstField:pub} (str:line) -> str
123	    §E{}
124	    §B{i:i32} (indexof line "," :ordinal)
125	    §IF{if1} (< i 0)
126	      §R line
127	    §R (substr line 0 i)
128	```
129	
130	```calor
131	§M{m5:Collections}
132	  §F{f1:Tally:pub} (str:key) -> i32
133	    §E{mut,alloc}
134	    §DICT{counts:str:i32}
135	    §/DICT{counts}
136	    §PUT{counts} key 1
137	    §R §IDX counts key
138	```
139	
140	```calor
141	§M{m6:Effects}
142	  §F{f1:Greet:pub} (str:name) -> void
143	    §E{cw}
144	    §C{Console.WriteLine} §A "Hello" §/C
145	    §C{Console.WriteLine} §A name §/C
146	```
147

Real example from `docs/design/spikes/effect-rows/after/A3-middleware.calr`:

  §C{Console.WriteLine} §A "Hello" §/C

## 3. Effect polymorphism — `<eff e>` and `§E{e}`, and interface-vs-impl checking

This is the core of your question, and the compiler has a real, enforced answer.

- `<eff e>` after the method-id braces declares an **effect variable** `e` (an effect-row type parameter), analogous to a generic type parameter but for effects.
- `§E{e}` in the signature attaches the effect row `e` to a **function-typed parameter** (e.g. `Func<i32>:next §E{e}` or `RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>:next §E{e}`), meaning "whatever effects the delegate `next` performs."
- `§E{e}` as the body's effect line means "this method performs exactly the effects of `e` and no more" — the method is polymorphic over the callee's effects.

```calor

  §MT{mt001:Handle}<eff e> (i32:request, Func<i32>:next §E{e}) -> i32

  §IMPL{IPipelineBehavior}

    §E{e}
    §R §C{RunTwice} §A next §/C

Alpha-equivalence holds: the impl may rename the variable (`after/A3-middleware-alpha.calr` uses `<eff f>` / `§E{f}` and still compiles) — the compiler records effect variables as binder indices, not names (`SPIKE-NOTES.md` S1).

'IPipelineBehavior.Handle' on class 'LoggingBehavior' declares effect(s) [cw]
not declared by the interface (interface declares: [pure]). An implementation
may not broaden the interface's declared effect set — interface dispatch
launders effects identically to overrides.
```

It may NOT introduce a concrete effect like `cw`. The escape hatch is the effect-polymorphic interface itself (`<eff e>` + `§E{e}` on the interface method), which is exactly the mechanism you found. Caveat from `SPIKE-NOTES.md` "R2's residual": member-level `eff` checking only works when BOTH interface and impl are Calor-declared; a C#-declared interface has no row to check against.

```calor

§P "before"                                                // shorthand print line
```

```calor

§P (+ "  " (+ entry (+ " — " problem)))
§R (+ name (+ "|" §C{stamp.ToString} §/C))
§R (+ "catalog[" (+ §C{content.Length.ToString} §/C "]"))
```

```calor

```

or with the print shorthand: `§P (+ "pre:" §C{request.ToString} §/C)`. (For many string types you can concatenate the object directly: `(+ "pre:" request)` works when the RHS is already string-typed.)

From `after/A2.calr` (this file compiles clean — `A2.diagnostics.txt`):

- `§AMT{m008:Handle:pub}<eff e> (…) -> TResponse` — **async** method, id `m008`, name `Handle`, public, effect-polymorphic over `e`. - `§E{e}` (body's first line) — effect declaration: performs exactly the effects of variable `e`.

// await processor.Process(request, cancellationToken)

Alpha-equivalence holds: the impl may rename the variable (`after/A3-middleware-alpha.calr` uses `<eff f>` / `§E{f}` and still compiles) — the compiler records effect variables as binder indices, not names (`SPIKE-NOTES.md` S1).

**Does an interface method with NO effect force pure implementations? YES.** The compiler forbids an implementation from BROADENING the interface's effect set. Two real failing fixtures prove it:

`after/A3-middleware-broadening.calr` — interface declares polymorphic `§E{e}`, impl adds `cw` via `§E{e, cw}` and a `§P "before"`. Result (diagnostics file, `exit 1`):

```

'IPipelineBehavior.Handle' on class 'LoggingBehavior' declares effect(s) [cw]
not declared by the interface (interface declares: [pure]). An implementation
may not broaden the interface's declared effect set — interface dispatch
launders effects identically to overrides.
```

`after/A2-broadening.calr` (the MediatR case) — same `Calor0421` plus `Calor0410: Function 'Handle' uses effect 'unknown' but does not declare it`.

It may NOT introduce a concrete effect like `cw`. The escape hatch is the effect-polymorphic interface itself (`<eff e>` + `§E{e}` on the interface method), which is exactly the mechanism you found. Caveat from `SPIKE-NOTES.md` "R2's residual": member-level `eff` checking only works when BOTH interface and impl are Calor-declared; a C#-declared interface has no row to check against.

## 4. Calling methods / printing / string building

Calls: `§C{Obj.Method} §A arg1 §A arg2 §/C` — each arg prefixed `§A`, list closed with `§/C`. Parameterless call needs no args and no `§/C` in practice (`§C{next}`). Print statement: `§P expr` (auto-charges `cw`).

```calor
§C{Console.WriteLine} §A "Hello from Calor E2E Test!" §/C   // 01_hello_world.calr
§P "before"                                                // shorthand print line
```

String concatenation is the prefix `+` operator (NOT a method); `+` on strings concatenates. `ToString` is a normal call. Real lines from the corpus:

```calor
§C{Console.WriteLine} §A (+ STR:"Sending email to: " to) §/C
§P (+ "  " (+ entry (+ " — " problem)))
§R (+ name (+ "|" §C{stamp.ToString} §/C))
§R (+ "catalog[" (+ §C{content.Length.ToString} §/C "]"))
```

So to build `"pre:" + request.ToString()` and print it:

```calor
§C{Console.WriteLine} §A (+ "pre:" §C{request.ToString} §/C) §/C
```

or with the print shorthand: `§P (+ "pre:" §C{request.ToString} §/C)`. (For many string types you can concatenate the object directly: `(+ "pre:" request)` works when the RHS is already string-typed.)

## 5. Token meanings in your snippet

From `after/A2.calr` (this file compiles clean — `A2.diagnostics.txt`):

- `§AMT{m008:Handle:pub}<eff e> (…) -> TResponse` — **async** method, id `m008`, name `Handle`, public, effect-polymorphic over `e`. - `§E{e}` (body's first line) — effect declaration: performs exactly the effects of variable `e`.
- `§EACH{each009:processor:var} _preProcessors` — foreach over `_preProcessors`, loop var named `processor`, id `each009`. The `:var` marks the loop variable as inferred-type (`var`). (Exemplar shows the simpler `§EACH{id:x} coll`; `§EACHKV{id:k:v} dict` for dictionaries.)

Type annotation is optional (`§B{name}` vs `§B{name:type}`). `§B{_}` binds to a throwaway.
- `§AWAIT …` — awaits a Task-valued expression.
- `§R expr` — return (`§R` bare = void return).
- `§FLD{Seq<IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest>>:_preProcessors:priv:readonly}` — field: `§FLD{Type:name:visibility:modifiers}`. Here private readonly.

## 6. Awaiting a Task directly (no ConfigureAwait)

`§AWAIT` takes any Task expression directly. Direct await of a call with a bare arg is confirmed by a real line: `§B{_} §AWAIT §C{Task.Delay} 100`. So:

```calor
// await processor.Process(request, cancellationToken)
§B{_} §AWAIT §C{processor.Process} §A request §A cancellationToken §/C

// return await next()
§R §AWAIT §C{next}
```

`ConfigureAwait(false)` in A2 is written as `§AWAIT §C{expr.ConfigureAwait} false` — it is just a normal method call being awaited, not special syntax. You do not need it.
